# PALW LLM proof-of-work — blocks generated by inference, and independently replayed

**Date:** 2026-08-16 · **Branch:** `palw-llm-pow-unified` · **Network:** devnet (`algo_id = 4`)
**Harness:** `scripts/misaka-palw-pow-e2e.sh` with `PALW_REAL=1` (no fixture)
**Runtime:** pinned Qwen3.5-2B-Q4_K_M via `palw-worker`, Metal profile

The Ambient-inspired half of the design, running: a block's proof of work **is** an LLM
inference, and a second node re-runs that inference to accept the block.

## 1. What actually happens per block

```
pre_pow_hash ‖ timestamp ‖ nonce ‖ network_id
   → palw_pow_seed_v1  (keyed BLAKE2b-256)
   → palw_pow_prompt_v1  "MISAKA PALW proof-of-work v1\nseed: <64 hex>\ncontinue:"
   → palw-worker --mode verify --prompt-stdin --n-predict 128   ← the work
   → projection (output_commitment, gemm_trace_root, canonical_compute_units, …)
   → palw_l1_tag_from_projection → Layer-1 tag → Layer-0 finalizer → header PoW
```

Both grindable header inputs (`timestamp` AND `nonce`) are inside the *expensive* computation,
not merely inside the cheap finalizer — a miner cannot re-roll the timestamp to dodge the
inference.

Single invocation reproduced by hand (seed = `abab…`, cold process):

```
decode_tokens             79          (EOG before the 128 budget — real generation)
canonical_compute_units   681
gemm_trace_root           a6b44f727bc1385b1d4d2423fe127a7b…
wall                      9.5 s cold / ~2.3 s warm (page cache + tag cache)
```

## 2. Measured runs

| run | blocks | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 6 blocks | 6 | **PASS** — mined, node-1 accepted all 6 over p2p by independent replay, node-2 fail-loud fired |
| 20 blocks + IBD | 20 | mined; node-1 accepted 20 by independent replay; **a fresh node-3 replayed the whole chain from genesis** |

### The from-genesis leg, and the harness bug it exposed

A fresh node-3 (its own worker, no state) synced the whole chain and validated every header by
re-running the inference:

```
IBD: Processed 20 block headers (100%)
IBD: Processed 20 block bodies  (100%)
IBD with peer 127.0.0.1:37711 completed successfully
Processed 20 blocks … (20 UTXO-validated blocks)
[ibd-perf] validate(A,parallelizable) 955565.7us      ← 0.96 s per header
```

That 0.96 s per header **is** the PALW inference on the replay path — the cost a late joiner
pays to verify the chain, visible in the node's own performance counter.

The first run of this leg nonetheless printed FAIL: `count_ibd` matched
`IBD: Processed N blocks`, while the node logs `N block headers` / `N block bodies`. The
counter returned 0 through a perfectly successful sync and the harness failed the run on its
own regex. Fixed (bodies are the real measure, headers the fallback) and verified against the
recorded log before re-running — a harness that can fail a good run is a harness that will
eventually pass a bad one.

Re-run with the fix, full verdict:

```
verified : node-1 accepted 20 blocks over p2p (independent PALW replay)
verified : node-2 (no worker, no fixture) hit the designed fail-fast
verified : node-3 caught up from genesis (20 blocks; independent PALW replay of the whole chain)
PASS: 20 PALW blocks mined (devnet), independently replay-validated, and synced.
```

Per-header replay cost on the joining node held at 0.86–0.96 s across the run.

Cadence of the 6-block run (real inference, devnet trivial bits ⇒ ~1 attempt/block):

```
13:23:54.139  daa 0      13:24:01.341  daa 3
13:23:56.446  daa 1      13:24:05.609  daa 4
13:23:58.785  daa 2      13:24:07.839  daa 5
```

≈ 2.3–4.3 s per block, i.e. the block interval on this network is *the model's decode time*,
which is the entire point of the scheme. (A fixture run mines these in microseconds; the timing
alone separates the two modes.)

## 3. The three properties the harness proves

1. **Inference produces blocks.** node-0 mines only through the PALW path; `mode: REAL model
   via worker` and the per-block seconds establish that no fixture was in play.
2. **Inference re-produces the same tag on another host.** node-1 runs its own worker and
   accepts every block — the determinism class doing its job at the PoW layer, not just in the
   v2 trace work.
3. **A node without the runtime fails loudly, never silently.** node-2, started with
   `PALW_WORKER` / `MISAKA_PALW_GGUF` / the fixture flag all scrubbed, refuses at the startup
   rail:

   > `network devnet validates PALW (algo_id = 4) LLM proof-of-work, which needs the pinned
   > worker runtime. Set PALW_WORKER=… and MISAKA_PALW_GGUF=…, or export
   > MISAKA_PALW_POW_FIXTURE=1 for the model-free devnet fixture.`

   The alternative — a node that quietly rejects valid blocks and bans honest peers — is the
   failure this rail exists to prevent.

## 4. Scope, stated plainly

* **devnet only.** `pow_palw_activation` is `always()` in `DEVNET_PARAMS` and `never()` in
  mainnet/testnet/simnet. This run does not enable PALW anywhere else.
* This is the **Layer-1 PoW** lane (ADR-0021's subject, superseded for reward/activation). The
  verification stack built alongside it — v2 trace, legs, refutations, scheduling, carriage —
  is a *different* lane and remains consensus-inert.
* Difficulty is the devnet trivial `0x207fffff`, so one attempt wins a block. On a real
  difficulty the same work repeats per nonce, which is the cost model the economics assume.
